SQL for the species lookup of the species x hex x count table

Source: R/species.R
obis_h3_species_lookup_sql.Rd

One row per aphiaid in occ_h3: aphiaid BIGINT, name_key INTEGER, species, genus, family, "order", class, phylum, lineage BIGINT[], records BIGINT.

Usage

obis_h3_species_lookup_sql(from = "occ_h3", taxon = "taxon", max_depth = 64L)

Arguments

from

the species-level table (default "occ_h3").

taxon

the WoRMS taxon table (taxonID, parentNameUsageID), or NULL.

max_depth

guard against a cycle in the taxonomy (default 64).

Value

a SQL string (a SELECT, ordered by aphiaid).

Details

name_key is a dense integer per distinct species name (ordered by name): richness counts species names, as h3t and .h3t_indicators_sql() group by occ_h3.species, and some names carry several aphiaids (2,140 in the 2026-10 global store), so counting aphiaids would overstate sp.

lineage is the aphiaid itself followed by its ancestors, walked up taxon.parentNameUsageID from the occurrence's own aphiaid (accepted or not), so list_contains(lineage, A) selects exactly the aphiaids the recursive CTE of h3t / obis_taxon_children() finds walking down from A. A synonym keeps its own parent chain, not its accepted name's. Without a taxon table (taxon = NULL) the lineage is the aphiaid alone. The rank columns and the name are taken once per aphiaid (MIN, so a NULL class is replaced by a named one if both occur); records is summed over the coarsest occ_h3 tier.

Examples

cat(obis_h3_species_lookup_sql())
#> WITH RECURSIVE sp AS (
#>   SELECT aphiaid::BIGINT AS aphiaid, MIN(species) AS species, MIN(genus) AS genus,
#>          MIN(family) AS family, MIN("order") AS "order", MIN(class) AS class,
#>          MIN(phylum) AS phylum, SUM(records)::BIGINT AS records
#>   FROM occ_h3
#>   WHERE res = (SELECT MIN(res) FROM occ_h3) AND aphiaid IS NOT NULL
#>   GROUP BY 1),
#> up AS (
#>   SELECT aphiaid, aphiaid AS node, 0 AS depth FROM sp
#>   UNION ALL
#>   SELECT up.aphiaid, t.parentNameUsageID::BIGINT AS node, up.depth + 1 AS depth
#>   FROM up JOIN taxon t ON t.taxonID = up.node
#>   WHERE t.parentNameUsageID IS NOT NULL AND t.parentNameUsageID <> t.taxonID
#>     AND up.depth < 64),
#> lin AS (SELECT aphiaid, list(node ORDER BY depth)::BIGINT[] AS lineage FROM up GROUP BY aphiaid)
#> SELECT sp.aphiaid, (dense_rank() OVER (ORDER BY sp.species))::INTEGER AS name_key,
#>        sp.species, sp.genus, sp.family, sp."order", sp.class, sp.phylum,
#>        lin.lineage, sp.records
#> FROM sp JOIN lin USING (aphiaid)
#> ORDER BY sp.aphiaid
